reference.wait_instrumentation: baseline clock unchanged; elapsed duration includes waits

comparison_analysis.method: Retained raw evidence re-compared after excluding the exact libtest 60-second entrypoint notice from stdout comparison. Original output, elapsed durations, operation traces and repository snapshots remain unchanged.

method_notes: The reference is the pinned Rust revision preceding the submission redesign; the candidate includes that redesign and the six follow-up corrections.
The 1-commit and 10-commit workloads have three paired samples with reversed middle-sample order; each 50-commit and 100-commit workload has one paired scale probe.
One scenario runs at a time; all compilation and acceptance suites completed before collection.
Both applications use ordinary release compilation, isolated repositories and the same loopback service model.
The default full-stack footer is used; compact presentation has independent algorithmic and protocol assertions.
Elapsed durations include baseline waits. Baseline wait fields are null because its unchanged clock has no separate wait instrumentation.
HTTP counts exclude requests hidden inside the reference GitHub CLI. Native child publication is modelled by the fixture; installed-extension latency is not measured.
The candidate source and executable identities precede the mandatory commit-hook version increment.
The collection measures the complete redesign against the earlier Rust implementation and does not isolate the marginal timing effect of the six follow-up corrections.
Repeated samples provide descriptive medians and maxima, not confidence intervals or live-service latency forecasts; larger single-sample probes establish no latency distribution.
